title: Array API mixed inputs: encode y to integer codes, then move it to X's namespace/device ("everything follows X")
answers: LinearDiscriminantAnalysis fails when y is on a different device than X
how to support string labels with array API inputs in a classifier
check_array_api_mixed_inputs xfail, how do I make an estimator pass it
y from numpy, X from torch cuda raises an error in fit
body:
Symptom: with array_api_dispatch on, fitting a classifier whose `y` comes from a different namespace/device than `X` (e.g. numpy `y`, torch-GPU `X`), or whose `y` holds string labels, raises an error.
Root cause: fit code compared or used `y` directly against arrays in X's namespace (e.g. `xp.unique_counts(y)`, `X[y == group]`). Strings can't be represented in any array API namespace.
Fix pattern (sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit): `self.classes_ = unique_labels(y)` on the original `y`, then `y_encoded = move_to(_encode(y, uniques=self.classes_), xp=xp, device=array_device(X))`. Downstream code uses only `y_encoded` (integer codes that index `classes_`). `classes_` stays in y's namespace/device.
Constraints: any later step that uses `classes_` together with X-side arrays has to move it explicitly first. When an estimator gains this support, delete its `check_array_api_mixed_inputs` / `check_array_api_string_and_numeric_inputs` entries from `PER_ESTIMATOR_XFAIL_CHECKS` in sklearn/utils/_test_common/instance_generator.py so the common checks actually run. Add changelog fragments under doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/array-api/.
applies: Classifiers in sklearn that are adding array API support for mixed namespace/device or string targets
